We need to analyze these four options and find which one deviates conceptually from the others. The options are couplets (two lines each). Let me parse them:

Option 1:
"ناکس تربیت نشود ای حکیم کس - شمشیر نیک از آهن بد چون کند کسی؟"

This seems to be saying: "O wise one, no one can train a worthless person" and "How can a good sword be made from bad iron?" The concept is about inherent nature - some people/things cannot be improved through training/effort.

Option 2:
"که چو تر شد پلیدتر باشد - سگ به دریای هفت گانه بشوی"

This says: "Wash a dog in the seven seas, so that when it gets wet, it becomes more impure." This is a proverbial expression about how some things/people cannot be purified or improved - their nature remains bad.

Option 3:
"به سعی اندر او تربیت گم شود - ز وحشی نیاید که مردم شود"

This says: "Through effort, training is lost in him" and "He does not come from wildness to become civilized." Again, about inherent nature being unchangeable.

Option 4:
"پی نیکان گرفت و مردم شد - سگ اصحاب کهف روزی چند"

This says: "The dog of the People of the Cave took the path of the good and became human/civilized." This is a reference to the story of the Seven Sleepers (Ashab al-Kahf) where a dog became noble through association with good people. This suggests that nature CAN be changed through good company.

So options 1, 2, and 3 all express the idea that inherent nature cannot be changed - a bad person/thing cannot be improved through training or effort. Option 4 expresses the opposite: that even a dog can become noble through association with good people.

Therefore, option 4 is the deviant one.
